questions.question: What does a list in ServiceNow display?

options.text: A single record from a table
Records from a table where each row is a record and each column is a field
Only the fields marked as mandatory

explanation.correct: A list shows records from a table. In both the core platform and workspace, each row is a record and each column is a field. Lists can be interacted with in various ways including filtering and sorting. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=5115a7d447335ad4ca332a81736d436e&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: A single record is displayed on a form, not a list. Lists show multiple records.
Lists show all configured fields, not just mandatory ones.
Configuration settings are managed in different modules, not in lists.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: A list shows records from a table. On the ServiceNow platform, lists can be interacted with in various ways. In both the core platform and workspace, each row is a record and each column is a field.

questions.question: What is the purpose of views in ServiceNow?

options.text: To delete records from the database
To display lists or forms in different ways for different user types
To import data from external sources

explanation.correct: Views allow users to display lists or forms in different ways. System administrators can create views for different user types, such as employee, self-service, and mobile users. The number of records stays the same, but field order may vary. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=5115a7d447335ad4ca332a81736d436e&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Views don't delete records; they only control how data is displayed.
Table creation is a separate administrative function.
Data import is handled by Import Sets, not views.

options.text: A method to delete multiple records at once
Collecting data from related tables via reference fields

explanation.correct: Dot-walking collects data from related tables via reference fields. It works in form layout, but not in form design. It's commonly used in form builder, list views, platform analytics, and Workflow Studio. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=5115a7d447335ad4ca332a81736d436e&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Deleting records is done through list editing or bulk delete, not dot-walking.
Authentication is managed separately and unrelated to dot-walking.
Workflow execution follows different patterns; dot-walking is about data relationships.

questions.question: What are the three parts of a filter condition in ServiceNow?

explanation.correct: A filter condition has three parts: Field (can include related tables), Operator (varies by field type, like 'greater than' for numbers), and Value (text entry or choice list based on field type). See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=5115a7d447335ad4ca332a81736d436e&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: While tables and records are concepts in ServiceNow, they're not the three parts of a filter condition.
User, Role, and Permission relate to security, not filter conditions.
These are common field types but not the components of a filter condition.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: A filter condition has three parts. Field-- able to be chosen based on user access, can include related tables. Operator-- varies by field type. Value-- text entry or choice list based on field.

questions.question: What is the difference between personalize list and configure list layout?

options.text: They are the same function with different names
Personalize list affects only the individual user; configure list layout affects everyone
Personalize list is for admins only; configure list layout is for all users
Personalize list is permanent; configure list layout is temporary

explanation.correct: Where the list layout configuration affects everyone, the personalize list modifies the layout of a list for an individual user. It does not affect the platform default. Personalization should be used for temporary situations. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=5115a7d447335ad4ca332a81736d436e&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: They have different scopes - one affects all users, one affects only the individual.
The distinction is about scope of changes, not user permissions.
Actually, personalization persists for the user, but system changes override it.

questions.question: A user has personalized their incident list view. Later, an administrator adds a new column to the default list view. What will happen for that user?

options.text: The user will automatically see the new column
The user will not see the new column until they choose 'reset to column defaults'
The user's personalization will be automatically deleted
The administrator's change will be rejected

explanation.correct: Any global changes that occur at the system level will not be reflected in a personalized list. If the system administrator configures a list view a user has personalized, they will not see those newly added default changes until they choose reset to column defaults. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=5115a7d447335ad4ca332a81736d436e&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Personalization overrides system defaults; users must manually reset to see new default columns.
User personalization is preserved; it just overrides the system view.
Admin changes are applied to the system default, they just don't override user personalizations.

questions.question: Where is the view name displayed on a list or form?

options.text: At the bottom of the page
In brackets beside the table or form title (unless it's the default view)

explanation.correct: The view name will appear in brackets beside the table or form title, unless it's the default view. This helps users identify which view they are currently using. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=5115a7d447335ad4ca332a81736d436e&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: View names are displayed near the title, not at the bottom of the page.
The Application Navigator shows modules and menus, not current view names.
User profile settings contain user preferences, not current view indicators.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: The view name will appear in brackets beside the table or form title, unless it's the default view.

questions.question: What does a form in ServiceNow display?

options.text: Information from a single record in a table

explanation.correct: Forms in ServiceNow show information from a single record in a table, and can be accessed through global search or lists. The form's content varies with the record type, and users can view or edit this content. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=a7d52b9847335ad4ca332a81736d43a3&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Forms show a single record; lists show multiple records.
Forms can contain both read-only and editable fields based on configuration.
System configuration has dedicated modules; forms display record data.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: Forms in ServiceNow show information from a single record in a table, and can be accessed through global search or lists.

questions.question: Which elements are included on ServiceNow forms? (Choose two)

explanation.correct: Forms include fields, sections, formatters, UI actions, and related lists. These elements enhance how users navigate and interact with forms. Import sets and scheduled jobs are separate functionalities. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=a7d52b9847335ad4ca332a81736d43a3&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Import sets are for data loading, not form elements.
Scheduled jobs run automated tasks, they're not form components.

source.excerpt: Forms include fields, sections, formatters, UI actions, and related lists. These elements enhance how users navigate and interact with forms.

questions.question: What happens when you navigate away from a form without saving changes?

options.text: You will be prompted to save or discard changes before reloading the form
Changes are lost without any warning

explanation.correct: When changing views or navigating away, you will be prompted to save or discard changes before reloading the form. This prevents accidental data loss. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=a7d52b9847335ad4ca332a81736d43a3&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: ServiceNow doesn't auto-save form changes; users must explicitly save.
ServiceNow provides warnings to prevent accidental data loss.
Navigating away doesn't change the form's editability.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: Changing views will prompt you to save or discard changes before reloading the form.

questions.question: What are the three ways to modify a form in ServiceNow?

options.text: Form Builder, Form Design, and Form Layout

explanation.correct: There are several ways to modify a form: Form Builder, Form Design, and Form Layout. Each provides different capabilities for form customization. Administrators should avoid adding the same editable field in multiple sections. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=a7d52b9847335ad4ca332a81736d43a3&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Import, Export, and Copy are data operations, not form modification methods.
These are CRUD operations on records, not form configuration tools.
These describe user interactions, not form modification methods.

questions.question: What is the purpose of templates in ServiceNow?

options.text: To pre-fill common field values when creating records

explanation.correct: Templates allow users to fill in the most common fields for a table, save it as a template, and make it available to users. Users can apply templates manually when creating records, or administrators can set scripts to apply them automatically. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=a7d52b9847335ad4ca332a81736d43a3&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Table creation is separate from templates.
Backups are handled by different system functions.
Reports are generated separately, not through templates.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: To use a template, fill in the most common fields for a table. Save it as a template, and make it available to users. Users can apply templates manually when creating records, or administrators can set scripts to apply them automatically.

questions.question: Why should only certain groups be allowed to create templates?

options.text: To avoid bypassing processes like mandatory fields and UI policies
To prevent users from seeing each other's data

explanation.correct: Only certain groups should create templates to avoid bypassing processes, like mandatory fields and UI policies, particularly for records using condition based flows or workflows. Templates can potentially skip validation rules if not properly controlled. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=a7d52b9847335ad4ca332a81736d43a3&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Storage is not the primary concern with template creation.
Data visibility is controlled by ACLs, not template permissions.
System performance is not significantly impacted by template creation.

source.excerpt: Only certain groups should create templates to avoid bypassing processes, like mandatory fields and UI policies, particularly for records using condition based flows or workflows.

questions.question: What happens when a user personalizes a form using the personalize form feature?

options.text: The changes affect all users on the platform
The personalized form will remain each time the user logs in
The changes are temporary and reset on logout

explanation.correct: The personalized form will remain each time the user logs in. Only fields configured to display are available in the personalize form menu. Mandatory fields cannot be hidden through personalization. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=a7d52b9847335ad4ca332a81736d43a3&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Personalization only affects the individual user, not all users.
Mandatory fields cannot be hidden through the personalize form feature.
Personalization persists across sessions for the user.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: The personalized form will remain each time the user logs in. Only fields configured to display are available in the personalize form menu.

questions.question: In Form Builder, which elements can administrators configure in the policies and rules section? (Choose two)

explanation.correct: In the Form Builder policies and rules section, administrators can configure UI policies, access control rules, client scripts, business rules, and workspace view rules. Database schemas and network settings are managed elsewhere. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=a7d52b9847335ad4ca332a81736d43a3&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Database schemas are managed through table configuration, not Form Builder.
Network settings are system-level configurations, not form-related.

course.moduleTitle: SNAF Module 3: Configure applications for business

source.excerpt: In the policies and rules section, administrators can configure UI policies, access control rules, client scripts, business rules, workspace view rules.
